canvas-01.description: The lower left quarter of the title and index page carries map sheet 1, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and framed by a heavy border. It covers the south side of the W.J. & S. R.R. (P.R.R.) at Mays Landing Station, where Mill Street crosses the tracks and continues south as Estellville Avenue. Post runs west from Mill Street along the railroad, and Longwood Avenue runs south parallel to Estellville Avenue before turning east to meet it at the foot of the sheet. The blocks between the two avenues are laid out in narrow house lots, most built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings. The Mays Landing Water Power Co. holds the land along the railroad: its Store House No. 1 stands west of Mill Street, and its weaving mill, with a watchman and power from the main plant, stands on the east side of Estellville Avenue. The station building and a water tank are on the north side of the tracks. The ground east of Estellville Avenue and west of Longwood Avenue is marked vacant beyond. The rest of the page (not part of this map) holds the key map at 800 ft to an inch, the water and fire department notes and the street index.
notes: Estellville Avenue is the modern Mill Street south of the railroad; Post and the north end of Longwood Avenue are the modern Longwood Avenue; the east-west leg of Longwood Avenue at the foot of the sheet lies on the modern Harding Highway.
The W.J. & S. R.R. (Newfield Branch) is abandoned; Mays Landing Station is gone.
The key map on the same page, at 800 ft to an inch, is not georeferenced.

Sheet 1. Title, key map (800 ft, not used), water and fire notes and street index on most of the page; the lower-left quarter is map sheet 1 at 100 ft: Estellville Av and Longwood Av south of the W.J.&S. R.R. (Mays Landing Station), Post, Mill St; Mays Landing Water Power Co weaving mill. One part (the key map is not a part). Placed on Longwood Av/Mill St (old Post/Estellville), Harding Hwy/Mill St and Harding Hwy/Longwood Av, plus the Longwood Av bend (hand-picked).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, at 50 ft to an inch, covers the south bank of the Great Egg Harbor River below the Lake Lenape dam, between Mill Street (also labelled Main) and the lake shore, south to the W.J. & S. R.R. Most of the sheet is the plant of the Mays Landing Water Power Co.: the cotton mill and factory buildings on the river (picker house, engine room, mill buildings making cotton goods), a hydro-electric station at the dam, a large fireproof reinforced concrete mill building built in 1924, a long row of brick warehouses on a siding, coal bins and tanks, and the company's warehouse at the railroad. Weymouth Road runs west from Mill Street past rows of frame dwellings; Minden and Dey are arbitrary names for unnamed streets near the warehouses. Along Mill Street stand the Union Hotel, an auto repair shop, the public school and frame dwellings, with stores and dwellings on the east side. Estellville Avenue is lettered at the railroad crossing in the lower right corner. The sheet notes that the mill information came from office plans and describes the private fire protection.
notes: Mill Street is labelled 'Mill (Main)'.
Minden and Dey are marked 'arbitrary' (names given by the map maker).

Weymouth Road at Mill Street lies near the modern Old Harding Highway junction, but the drawn road runs at a different angle; the modern junction was not used as control (about 17 m from where the sheet places it).
Mays Landing Water Power Co. mill building marked fireproof, built 1924.

Sheet 2, 50 ft. Mill St (Main) between the river and the W.J.&S. R.R., Weymouth Rd, Dey and Minden (arbitrary names); Mays Landing Water Power Co cotton mill and warehouses, Union Hotel, public school. One part. No usable junction: Weymouth Rd/Mill St lies about 17 m from the modern Old Harding Hwy/Mill St node. Placed (helmert, low confidence) on the Mill St pipe crossing at the north track carried from canvas-01, with a derived point turned so Mill St meets its position on sheet 3 at the river (north -30.5 deg, 4 deg off the neighbours).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3, at 50 ft to an inch, covers the west end of the business street: Mill Street from the bridge over the Great Egg Harbor River north-east past Main Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street to Hudson Street and Herbertown Road, with the shore of Lake Lenape along its west side. Main Street runs east from Mill Street to Hudson Street, with 2nd and 3rd Streets parallel to the north. The blocks are lined with frame dwellings, many of two storeys with porches, and their outbuildings; the lots between Mill Street and the lake run down to the water. Roy E. Beach's concrete-block and frame garage stands at the corner of Mill and Main Streets, an auto and bicycle repair shop on 2nd Street, an ice house and a boat house on the river bank, and a plumber's shop on 3rd Street. South of Main Street the lots run to the river. The north edge of the sheet is marked as the edge of sheet 7, the east edge as sheet 4 and the foot as sheet 2.
notes: Mill Street north of Main Street is now Lenape Avenue (and North Mill Street at its south end); 2nd Street between Mill and Hudson Streets is now Heritage Lane.
Hudson Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street are drawn about 20 ft wide, too narrow for the detector; their junctions were hand-picked.

Sheet 3, 50 ft. Mill St from Lake Lenape to Hudson St, 2nd and 3rd Sts, Main St to the Great Egg Harbor River; Roy E. Beach garage. One part. Hudson, 2nd and 3rd Sts drawn 20 ft wide; four junctions hand-picked. 2nd St (Mill to Hudson) is now Heritage Lane; Mill St north of Main is Lenape Av.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, at 50 ft to an inch, covers the centre of the town between Hudson Street and Mistletoe Avenue: Main Street along the south, with Oak (Maple) running diagonally from Mill Street to Hanthorn Avenue, 2nd and 3rd Streets east of Hanthorn Avenue, and Abbott Avenue south of Main Street. Main Street carries the business block: the Central House, the Masonic Lodge, the First National Bank (brick), the Home Bakery, stores, a druggist and dwellings, with the M.E. Church on the north side and a cemetery behind it to the east. North of Main Street are large lots with frame dwellings and outbuildings along Hudson Street, Oak and Hanthorn Avenue; the land south of Main Street towards Abbott Avenue is swampy. Dry Run crosses the north-west corner beside Mill Street and Herbertown Road. The margins name sheet 7 at the top, sheet 3 to the west, sheet 5 to the east and sheet 6 to the south-east.
notes: Oak (Maple) is now Ken Scull Avenue; Mill Street here is now Lenape Avenue; Mistletoe is now Taylor Avenue.
Hanthorn Avenue / Main Street was not used: the modern junction is about 8 m from the drawn one.
Junctions on Main Street were hand-picked; the detector paired lot lines there.
M.E. Church, Masonic Lodge, Central House, First National Bank.

Sheet 4, 50 ft. Main St from Hudson St to Mistletoe, Oak (Maple), Hanthorn Av, 2nd and 3rd Sts, Abbott Av; M.E. Church, First National Bank, Central House, cemetery. One part. Oak (Maple) is Ken Scull Av; Mistletoe is Taylor Av. Main St junctions hand-picked; Hanthorn Av/Main St left out (8 m off).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, at 50 ft to an inch, covers the county seat blocks between Cape May Avenue and Farragut Avenue, from Main Street north to 4th Street, with Grove running east from Cape May Avenue. The block between Main Street, Grove, 2nd Street and Farragut Avenue holds the Atlantic County buildings: the court house, the clerk's and surrogate's offices (brick), the jail with its kitchens, and the sheriff's dwelling. St. Vincent de Paul R.C. Church stands at Cape May Avenue and 2nd Street, the Presbyterian church on Main Street west of Cape May Avenue, and the fire department near 2nd Street. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings on large lots, with a large vacant block between 2nd and 3rd Streets and narrow house lots laid out between 3rd and 4th Streets. The foot of the sheet repeats the south side of Main Street with the openings of Mistletoe Avenue and Cape May Avenue (sheet 6). Neighbouring sheets 7, 8, 4 and 9 are named in the margins.
notes: Grove is now Parsons Row.
3rd Street meets Farragut Avenue at a jog; both modern nodes were used, one for each drawn corner.
County buildings: court house, jail, sheriff's office and dwelling, clerk's and surrogate's offices.
St. Vincent de Paul R.C. Church; Presbyterian church; fire department.

Sheet 5, 50 ft. Cape May Av and Farragut Av between Main and 4th St, 2nd and 3rd Sts, Grove; County buildings (court house, jail), St. Vincent de Paul R.C. Church, Presbyterian church, fire department. One part. Grove is Parsons Row. Fitted 7.79 px/ft, 2.4 percent below the atlas value.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6, at 50 ft to an inch, covers the town south of Main Street between Mistletoe Avenue and Farragut Avenue (Railroad Avenue), across the W.J. & S. R.R. to the Great Egg Harbor River. On Main Street are stores, a garage of concrete block with capacity for 30 cars, a moving picture house, the post office and offices, and the brick American Hotel east of Farragut Avenue. Court House Station of the railroad stands at Farragut Avenue. North of the railroad the lots along Mistletoe and Cape May Avenues hold frame dwellings and outbuildings; south of it Cape May Avenue continues to the river, with Gaskill running between Cape May and Farragut Avenues. The south end of the sheet is laid out in narrow lots running down to the river, which curves around the east and west sides of the sheet.
notes: Cape May Avenue south of Main Street is now Pennington Avenue (offset from Cape May Avenue north of Main Street); Mistletoe Avenue is now Taylor Avenue; the modern Harding Highway cuts through the blocks between them.
Farragut Avenue is labelled (Railroad Avenue).
American Hotel, post office, Court House Station of the W.J. & S. R.R.
Placed with three detected junctions and two points carried from sheet 5; little control south of the railroad.

Sheet 6, 50 ft. South of Main St: Mistletoe, Cape May Av, Farragut (Railroad) Av, Gaskill, W.J.&S. R.R. and Court House station, to the Great Egg Harbor River; American Hotel, post office. One part. Cape May Av south of Main is Pennington Av; Mistletoe is Taylor Av. Three junctions plus two points carried from sheet 5; weak south of the railroad.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7, at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-west part of the town plan: the grid of Adams, Bainbridge, Calhoun, Decatur and Cape May Avenues crossed by 3rd to 11th Streets, with Dry Run and Lake Lenape along the west side and Herbertown Road running north-west from Mill Street. Most blocks are platted into narrow building lots and are empty; dwellings stand only along Bainbridge and Calhoun Avenues between 7th and 9th Streets, along Herbertown Road, and in the blocks near Mill Street, Hanthorn Avenue and 3rd Street at the south-east corner, where the Elkton Burch saw mill (steam power) stands. West of Dry Run the land is divided into large tracts. The margins name sheets 3, 4 and 5 at the foot and sheet 8 to the east.
notes: Herbertown Road is now Park Road; Mill Street here is now Lenape Avenue; Calhoun Avenue is now Calhoun Street.
8th and 10th Streets west of Adams Avenue are not in the modern street network.
Elkton Burch saw mill.

Sheet 7, 100 ft. Adams, Bainbridge, Calhoun, Decatur and Cape May Avs, 3rd to 11th Sts, Herbertown Rd, Dry Run, Lake Lenape; Elkton Burch saw mill. Mostly unbuilt lots. One part. Herbertown Rd is Park Road. 25 junctions.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8, at 100 ft to an inch, covers the north-east part of the town plan between Cape May Avenue and Babcocks Creek: Farragut, Perry, Lincoln, Cleveland and Garfield Avenues crossed by 3rd to 11th Streets, with Babcock Terrace curving along the east side. Nearly all of it is platted into narrow building lots with few buildings; dwellings stand mainly along Cape May Avenue and on 9th and 7th Streets, and a vacant factory stands at Perry Avenue and 9th Street. Lake Colwell lies in the north-west corner and Babcocks Creek winds south across the sheet, cutting through the platted blocks. The foot of the sheet repeats 3rd Street with the openings of Linwood and Laurel Avenues on sheet 9, and the corner block bounded by 4th Street and Cape May and Farragut Avenues is marked as sheet 5.
notes: Perry, Lincoln, Cleveland and Garfield Avenues and Babcock Terrace are not in the modern street network; control is on Cape May and Farragut Avenues only.
Vacant factory at Perry Avenue and 9th Street.

Sheet 8, 100 ft. Cape May, Farragut, Perry, Lincoln, Cleveland and Garfield Avs, 3rd to 11th Sts, Babcock Terrace, Babcocks Creek, Lake Colwell. Mostly unbuilt lots. One part. Perry, Lincoln, Cleveland, Garfield Avs and Babcock Terrace are not in the modern network; control on Cape May and Farragut Avs.

sheet-9-1.description: Sheet 9, at 100 ft to an inch and turned on the page (north towards the upper right), covers the south-east end of the town: Main Street running south from Farragut Avenue past the W.J. & S. R.R., across Babcock's Creek to River Road, with 2nd and 3rd Streets and Linwood and Laurel Avenues east of Farragut Avenue. Mays Landing High School stands on Farragut Avenue at 2nd Street. North of the creek, frame dwellings and an auto repair shop line Main Street, and platted lots fill the blocks between 2nd and 3rd Streets. South of the creek, Main Street meets River Road, the Boulevard runs south-east beside the railroad, and Absecon Avenue and Gravely Road (Wausau Lane) branch south, lined with scattered dwellings. The Great Egg Harbor River forms the west side of the sheet. The inset of the Atlantic Brick Mfg Co. works in the lower right corner is a separate part (not placed).
notes: Main Street at River Road is placed on the modern Old River Road / Somers Point Road junction; the Boulevard is roughly the modern Harding Highway and Gravely Road the modern Somers Point Road.
Linwood Avenue was not used: the modern Linwood Street lies about 16 m from the drawn one.
Mays Landing High School.
Control is three junctions on Farragut Avenue and one hand-picked point at River Road; low confidence south of the creek.

Sheet 9, 100 ft. Main St south of Farragut Av across Babcocks Creek, 2nd and 3rd Sts, Linwood and Laurel Avs, River Rd, Boulevard, Absecon Av, Gravely Rd (Wausau Lane), W.J.&S. R.R.; Mays Landing High School. Two parts: part 1 main map, part 2 inset at lower right (Atlantic Brick Mfg Co works, own north arrow). Part 1 placed on three Farragut Av junctions and Main St/River Rd taken as Old River Rd/Somers Point Rd (hand-picked); Linwood St left out (modern street about 16 m from the drawn one). Part 2 not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Atlantic Brick Mfg Co works (kilns, brick making, clay storage, R.R. sidings), drawn apart with its own north arrow (no street junction or other feature shared with the modern data; the sidings and the works are gone; needs a surveyed point on the works site or the old siding (aerial or historic topographic map); the key map at 800 ft to an inch is too coarse).
